confirmed.quality_sample_unit: unique canonical question; not a timing repeat or label rotation

two_stage_policy_204.new_inference: none; reuses the #171 data (calibration run-calibration250b decision_dense; test run-test2 core arms; run-cap2048 reasoning re-run)
two_stage_policy_204.known_at_declaration: Only the aggregate #171 results published in #171 and PRs #193/#203: direct 67.8 %, reasoning 65.4 % (cap 512) / 79.0 % (cap 2048, 87 still capped), reasoning 97.3 % where it finished under 512 tokens, direct 75.9 % on those and 51.2 % on the capped 164, test ECE 0.037 after T. The joint distribution of test-set direct confidence and either arm's correctness had not been computed or inspected. The thresholds below use calibration data only.
two_stage_policy_204.policy: Two-stage: always run chat_direct decision_selected (bit-identical to decision_dense). Let c = max option probability after temperature scaling with the #171 calibration fit (T = 1.05460455763381, binding of binary bf8fa083...). If c >= threshold, answer with the direct argmax; otherwise run chat_reasoning generate_long at cap 2048 and answer with its parsed letter (capped or unparseable counts as wrong, as in #171). Ties (c exactly at the threshold) answer directly.

primary.rule: Target direct-answer precision 0.95 on the calibration split: threshold = the smallest calibration confidence t such that, for every calibration confidence t' >= t whose accepted set {c >= t'} holds at least 25 questions (10 % of calibration), the calibration precision of that accepted set is >= 0.95.
primary.why_0_95: Reasoning that finishes is about 97 % accurate (#171), so direct answers at about 95 % precision should cost well under 2 pp in total when they cover a minority of questions. Chosen from the published #171 aggregates, not from test-set confidences.

secondary_fixed_coverage.rule: Route the least-confident fraction q of the calibration split to reasoning: threshold = sorted calibration confidences [round(q * 250)] (0-based, ascending); questions with c >= threshold answer directly. Reported with the same statistics as the primary but secondary: the decision rests on the primary only.

two_stage_policy_204.reference: always-reasoning at cap 2048 on the same 500 test questions (cap-512 outputs for the 336 finished, re-run outputs for the 164 capped; equivalent by #171 amendment 3)
two_stage_policy_204.comparison: paired policy-minus-reasoning accuracy with metrics.paired_quality (exact Clopper-Pearson for gains and losses, Bonferroni, conservative joint 95 % interval), margin 2 pp. Routed questions are concordant by construction.

capped_handling.as_measured: the 87 answers still capped at 2048 count as wrong in both the policy (when routed) and the reference; this is the reported primary figure.
capped_handling.pessimistic_bound: additionally recompute with every still-capped reasoning answer counted as correct in both arms (a completed reasoning answer that is always right). This can only help the reference where the policy answered directly; non-inferiority is called established only if the lower bound is >= -2 pp in both the as-measured and the pessimistic computation.

two_stage_policy_204.cost_accounting: Per question: 1 direct call always, plus 1 reasoning call when routed. Tokens: direct prompt tokens, plus reasoning prompt tokens and generated tokens when routed (no prefix or KV reuse between the two calls is assumed). Time: the measured selected-row call time plus the measured reasoning time (cap 2048) when routed; report sum, mean, p50, p95 and the ratio to always-reasoning. Sustained-load Metal figures as in #171.
two_stage_policy_204.exploratory: An accuracy/cost curve over a range of routed fractions computed on the test set is descriptive only and must not be used to choose the policy.
two_stage_policy_204.decision_grade_if: The primary threshold is fixed from calibration data before any test-set evaluation, so the test estimate for it is unbiased. Calibration-split reasoning outputs would only be needed to pick a different threshold by a rule that depends on reasoning accuracy (e.g. the cheapest threshold whose estimated loss is under the margin).

result.conclusion: Reasoning-level accuracy (margin narrowly not established) at 97 % of reasoning's time; the confident questions are the ones reasoning answers cheaply. #26 should not build on this policy.

amendments.change: Calibration reduced from the frozen 750 questions to a 250-question label-independent subject-stratified sample of them (tools/sample_decision_cases.py, seed geist-decision-calibration-sample-v1), and run with decision_dense only.
amendments.arms_reason: Temperature is fitted on chat_direct decision_dense logits only. decision_selected is bit-identical to decision_dense (checked on every paired trial of the test run), and scorealt_dense is a parity reference. chat_reasoning has no option probabilities and was never run on calibration.
amendments.reason: The full campaign (about 56 chunks, about 20 h of shared Mac time, more at the measured prompt lengths) was too large. Calibration only fits a single temperature; 250 questions bound it well.
amendments.reuse: Calibration questions already completed under the earlier three-arm calibration run (same binary, model, tokenizer and policy binding) are imported if they fall in the sample; only their decision_dense samples are used.
amendments.earlier_calibration_run: 3 chunks + 1 interrupted chunk, 136+ questions with three arms; retained as raw evidence, not used beyond the import

amendments.superseded_inference: 11 test questions had run under the earlier design (all arms, two trials) when this was decided. They were stopped, not inspected and are not used; the raw files are kept apart (run-test-superseded-2trial). The reported test run starts from zero under this amendment.
change: One trial per arm (--repeats 0) instead of a first call plus one warm repeat.

Determinism spot-check: after the main run, a second independent trial (separate process) on 20 test questions chosen by select_stratified with seed geist-decision-determinism-spotcheck-v1 (label-independent; the question IDs are frozen in the run manifest); numeric arms must match bit-exactly, generation token-for-token.
Core arms only (--core-arms): chat_direct decision_dense and decision_selected, chat_reasoning generate_long (cap 512). Dropped: scorealt_dense, generate_1 and the whole cloze profile.
amendments.arms_reason: decision_dense gives the direct accuracy, the paired comparison and the calibration metrics; decision_selected carries the selected-vs-reasoning speedup and is checked bit-exact against dense on every question; generate_long is the reasoning baseline. scorealt_dense (independent reference parity), generate_1 (one-token generation) and cloze (a different prompt style) are not needed for the gate; none is mandatory in the frozen plan.
amendments.binary: --repeats 0 needed bench_decision to accept zero repeats (argument check only), which changes the binary hash. The calibration binding includes the binary, so calibration is re-run on the new binary (250 questions, decision_dense, one trial); the earlier fit (T=1.0546, binary e1dac74e) is superseded and kept as evidence only.
amendments.reason: Test phase at ~21 h of shared Mac time was too large; this design is ~6-7 h.
amendments.statistical_scope: 500 questions give an estimate of the direct-minus-reasoning accuracy difference with its conservative paired 95 % interval, not proof of the 2 pp non-inferiority margin; establishing that margin needs roughly 1500 or more questions (depends on the observed discordance).

amendments.change: Re-run the chat_reasoning arm with decode cap 2048 on the 164 test questions whose cap-512 answer hit the cap; direct arms unchanged. Same binary (bf8fa083...), model, prompt policy, Metal/FP32/greedy/one trial.

scope.order: 3 capped questions first (dry run for the time estimate), then 3 finished questions (determinism check), then the other 161 capped; both triples are the first by sha256([seed, question_id]) with seed geist-decision-cap2048-v1

amendments.equivalence: Generation is greedy and deterministic (the 20-question spot-check reproduced every arm bit-exactly), and the cap only truncates: a question that reached EOS before 512 tokens yields the identical output at cap 2048. Re-running only the 164 capped questions is therefore equivalent to a full cap-2048 run. Checked directly on 3 finished questions, whose cap-2048 generations must be byte-identical to their cap-512 ones.
amendments.combined_baseline: reasoning at cap 2048 = the cap-512 output for the 336 finished questions, the cap-2048 output for the 164 re-run ones; paired against the unchanged direct arm with the same conservative interval and 2 pp margin.
amendments.reason: A third of the cap-512 reasoning answers hit the cap; where reasoning finished it was 97.3 % accurate, so the cap-512 baseline is not a fair quality reference.

step_3_batched_decode_gate.question: Do B independent sequences stepped as one m-row pass (the #186/#221 small-row kernels) give >= 2x aggregate decode tokens/s over single-sequence decode at B = 8 on Bonsai 2 27B Metal?
step_3_batched_decode_gate.design: test-only prototype, no public API change: B = 1/2/4/8 sequences forked from different questions, greedy, per-step wall time over >= 64 steps after a cool start

amendments.declared_after: the step-1 run with 256-aligned cuts (run-step1) completed. Its results were inspected before this amendment, so this is a corrective re-measurement of the declared gate, not a fresh test.
amendments.finding: The declaration's alignment was wrong for this model. Bonsai 2 27B resolves a prefill chunk of 320 on Metal, not 256: the qwen35 family adds 64 rows for weights of 4 GiB and more (families/qwen35.c prefill_delta). Qwen3.5 0.8B, which phase 1 measured, resolves 256. The runner's check of the engine chunk against the declaration refused to finalize, as designed.
amendments.observed_with_256_cuts: 472/500 bit-identical option logits. All 28 mismatches (max |difference| <= 0.003) are questions whose prefix-plus-suffix split and joined single prefill differ in a final pass of <= 8 rows: the small-row PQ2_0 kernels of #186/#221 round differently from the large GEMM. The other 407 non-aligned questions and all 65 questions whose cut happened to be a multiple of 320 are bit-identical. Argmax 500/500 identical, accuracy 67.8 % in both arms, end-to-end time 0.385x of independent calls.
amendments.change: Re-run the decision_prefix arm only, with each subject's cut aligned down to 320 (tools/eval_decision_prefix.py --align 320 --reference-from run-step1). The reference is run-step1's decision_dense samples: same binary, model, cases, profile, backend, threads and environment, which the runner checks. Greedy scoring is deterministic across processes (#171 spot-check, 20/20 bit-identical).
amendments.gate: unchanged: option logits bit-identical on 500/500; accuracy identical; latency, end-to-end time, snapshot bytes and RSS reported
amendments.step_2: the fork check uses the engine's chunk too: cuts aligned to 320
amendments.budget: one lease: ~500 x 2.1 s + 57 prepares (~3 min) + model load, about 25 min

amendments.reason: At cap 2048 a capped full-reasoning answer counts as wrong, so early exit 'beats' full reasoning (33/200 calibration and 89/500 test answers capped). The tau 0.7 freeze (PR #269) and the held-out run started with it are superseded: the run was stopped after 420 questions (files kept as test-superseded-cap2048, not used).
amendments.cap_applies_to: both the full-reasoning baseline and the early-exit policy
amendments.memory_check: Bonsai 2 27B: trained context 262,144; FP32 KV 128 KiB per token (geist_model_plan); a session window of prompt (<= 3,033 tokens) + 8,192 + 2 is ~1.37 GiB of KV + ~150 MiB DeltaNet state; 9 sessions (8 slots + the prefix session) ~13.7 GiB, plus snapshot images (prefix <= 0.45 GiB, probe <= 1.5 GiB) and 6.7 GiB of weights: ~22.5 GiB on the 64 GB M1 Max. 8 in flight at cap 8192 fits.
amendments.constant_batch: tools/bench_reasoning_batch pad mode: every geist_session_decode_batch step has exactly 8 sessions; a finished question's slot keeps decoding (tokens discarded) until the next question takes it, and spare slots decode the first question's prompt. Each question's tokens then come only from 8-session steps, which the engine makes independent of the other members (bit for bit).
amendments.rerun_rule: Greedy determinism at fixed n = 8: a question whose earlier generation finished under 2048 using only 8-session steps keeps its output. Re-run at cap 8192: (a) every question capped at 2048, (b) every question that finished but had tokens from smaller batch steps (chunk tails before pad mode), (c) 8 finished all-8-step questions per set as a determinism spot-check (sha256([geist-cap8192-spotcheck-v1, question_id]) order), which must reproduce their earlier output token for token.
